A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 19-page JointDiT paper, including Appendices A–C. Text extraction and page rendering support a complete comparison; differences are confined to administrative first-page information and PDF metadata.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C report original JointDiT generation, depth-estimation, ablation and qualitative results.

after.justification: The same original JointDiT experiments and results remain in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical Flux-based architecture, depth branch, joint attention, adaptive scheduling weights, unbalanced timestep sampling and training objective.

E1.justification: All training and evaluation datasets and tasks remain unchanged, including the five depth benchmarks, image-generation evaluations and Appendix B.3 panorama generation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in every comparison. For example, Table 2 retains Readout-Guidance, ControlNet and UniCon, and Appendix Tables 6–7 retain the same image-generation and joint-generation baselines.

E3.justification: Dataset subsets, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets and testing procedures are identical. Both retain the 75k-iteration main training setup and Appendix A.1’s 20 denoising steps and guidance scale of 3.5.

E4.justification: The scheduling-weight and timestep-sampling ablations in Tables 3–4, LoRA-rank ablation in Table 8, and supplementary qualitative analyses are identical.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The result tables retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical result entries and qualitative findings match, including Appendix Tables 6–8. For example, Table 2 reports JointDiT FID 12.62 and AbsRel 6.99 in both versions.

T1.justification: The flow-matching formulation, joint conditional objective, adaptive-weight definitions and timestep-sampling mathematics in Equations 1–7 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about unified RGB-depth modeling, joint-generation quality and competitive conditional-task performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning the transformer image prior, ETH3D performance and Flux’s image-generation metrics remain identical. The limitation describing increased parameters and sampling time is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A preserve the same implementation, preprocessing, hyperparameter, hardware and training-time details. Project and training-code access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 and all 62 references are identical, preserving the same positioning relative to diffusion transformers and earlier joint and conditional generation methods.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 1 May 2025 to v2 dated 26 June 2025. The paper’s wording, headings and main-text/appendix organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–8 retain identical content, captions, structure and placement. Rendered pages match apart from the administrative version/date text in the first-page margin.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, supporting evidence, explanations, limitations and appendices are identical. Updating the version/date stamp, adding its self-link and changing PDF metadata do not meaningfully alter the paper’s clarity, reproducibility or evidential strength.
